description:
A SWML document for handling inbound SMS or MMS messages. The document has a top-level
`sections` map; execution starts at `sections.main`, and each section is an ordered array of
methods. Additional sections can be invoked via `execute`, `transfer`, or `goto`.

See the [Messaging SWML reference](/docs/swml/reference/messaging) for the full list of
available methods.
title: Messaging SWML Document

reply.description:
Create and send an outbound message in response to the inbound message. Accepts one of:
a string (used as the message body), an object with body, media, and routing fields, or
an inline `switch` that branches the reply on a variable value.

`reply` does not end execution — subsequent steps in the section continue to run after
the reply is queued.
reply.title: reply

receive.description: Accept the inbound message without sending a reply. No-op step.
receive.title: receive

url.description: Endpoint to call. Must be a publicly reachable URL.

headers.description: HTTP headers to include with the request, as a map of header name to value. Each value must be a string.

body.description:
Request body, always sent JSON-encoded. An object is sent as a JSON object. A
string is sent as a JSON string value, with quotes and escaping, not as raw text.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. Clamped to a maximum of `5.0`.

request.description:
Make an HTTP request from inside your SWML document — useful for looking up
records, calling your own API, or fetching data to use later in the message flow.

After the request, the `%{request_result}` variable tells you the outcome:

- `"success"` — the URL returned a 2xx response.
- `"failed"` — the URL returned a response outside the 2xx range, such as a 4xx
  or 5xx.
- `"timeout"` — the request didn't get a response within `timeout` seconds, or
  the connection to the URL failed.
- `"limit_exceeded"` — your document already made the maximum of 10 requests;
  this call was skipped.

Timeouts, connection failures, and unsuccessful HTTP responses don't stop your
document — the next steps still run, so you can branch on `%{request_result}` to
handle each outcome. Omitting `url`, or a `url` that expands to an empty value,
is a fatal error that stops the document.

When `save_variables` is `true` and the URL returns a 2xx response whose body is
a JSON object, the parsed fields are available as `%{request_response.<field>}`.
The response status code is in `%{request_response_code}` as a string (for
example `"200"`) and the response body in `%{request_response_body}`. The stored
body is a string, truncated to its first 65,536 characters after the response
is received; responses with a JSON content type are stored as re-serialized
JSON, so formatting can differ from what the server sent.
request.title: request

dest.description:
Where to execute. One of:

- The name of a section in the current document.
- A URL (`http` or `https`) that returns a messaging SWML document.
  SignalWire fetches it with a `POST` request.
- An inline messaging SWML document, supplied as a JSON string that contains
  a JSON object.

params.description: Parameters accessible as `params.*` in the called section or document. Replaces (does not merge with) any outer `params` from the caller.

execute.description:
Run a section, a SWML document fetched from a URL, or an inline SWML document as a
subroutine. Execution continues in the called section or document, then returns to
the caller when it completes — either via `return` or by reaching the end. A called
document starts at its `sections.main`.

Accepts either a destination string (shorthand) or an object with `dest` and
`params`. The shorthand calls the destination with empty `params`, and `%{...}`
references in it are not expanded; use the object form to build the destination
or pass parameters from variables.
execute.title: execute

dest.description:
Where to transfer. One of:

- The name of a section in the current document.
- A URL (`http` or `https`) to fetch the new SWML document from. Authentication
  can be embedded in the URL as `username:password@url`.
- An inline SWML document, supplied as a JSON string that contains a JSON object.
  A nested YAML or JSON object is not accepted. Execution starts at its
  `sections.main`.

`%{...}` variable references in `dest` are expanded before the destination is
resolved.

method.description: HTTP method for the fetch request. Used only when `dest` is a URL.

params.description:
Parameters for the transferred section or document, available there as `params.*`.
When `dest` is a URL, they are also sent in the request body. They replace the
current `params` rather than merging with them; when omitted, the target receives
an empty object.

String values are expanded for `%{...}` variable references at every depth,
including inside nested objects and arrays. Keys are not expanded. Each
substitution produces a string, a reference to a path that doesn't exist becomes
an empty string, and expressions are not evaluated.

transfer.description:
Hand processing over to another section, another SWML document fetched from a URL,
or an inline SWML document. `dest` selects which.

This is a tail call — it replaces the current document and does not return.
Steps after `transfer` are skipped, including steps in calling sections.

When `dest` is a URL, SignalWire sends the
[inbound message webhook payload](/docs/apis/rest/webhooks/inbound-message-webhook)
in the request body to `dest`, using `method` (`POST` by default): `message`
describes the original inbound message, `params` carries the values supplied here,
and `vars` carries the propagated runtime variables (`request_result`,
`reply_result`, etc.) accumulated by the current document.
transfer.title: transfer

variable.description:
Variable path to match. Specified without the `%{}` wrapper (e.g. `message.body`).
The resolved value is converted to a string, then transformed and compared exactly
with the `case` keys. A missing variable path resolves to an empty string.

transform.description: Transform to apply to the value before matching.

case.description:
Map of values to arrays of SWML methods to execute. The key is the value to compare
against `variable` (after applying `transform`); the value is the array of methods
to run on match. Keys are literal and are not transformed, and matching is exact.
An empty-string key matches a missing variable; otherwise `default` is used.

default.description:
Array of SWML methods to execute if no `case` matches. If omitted and no case
matches, execution stops with an error.

switch.description:
Branch on a variable's value, with optional text transforms applied before matching.
Useful for keyword-driven inbound message handling.

After the selected branch completes, execution normally continues with the next step
after `switch`, subject to the document execution limit and any control-flow change
or execution failure.
switch.title: switch

label.description: Label to jump to. Must reference a `label` step in the current section.

max.description:
Maximum number of jumps to `label`. Accepts an integer or a `%{...}` variable
reference; a reference is expanded and then converted to an integer. A reference
that doesn't resolve allows no jumps — it does not fall back to 100.

Jumps are counted per target label for the whole run, not per `goto` step: every
`goto` that targets the same label name shares one count, including `goto` steps
in other sections and in documents reached through `execute` or `transfer`. Each
jump attempt adds one to the count and is allowed while the count is at most this
step's `max`.

When an attempt exceeds `max`, the jump doesn't happen and the steps array that
contains the label ends without running its remaining steps. Execution continues
with whatever ran that array, such as the steps after an enclosing `switch` or
the caller of an `execute`.

`max` cannot raise the document's limit of 100 steps, which counts every step
including each `label` passed. That limit can stop execution before `max` jumps
are reached.

goto.description:
Jump to a named label in the current section. Used for retry loops and conditional
repetition. `goto` does not cross subroutine boundaries.

Accepts a label name as a string (shorthand) or an object with `label` and `max`.
The shorthand jumps to the label exactly as written, without variable expansion,
with the default `max` of 100.
goto.title: goto

return.description:
Return from the current section. Inside a subroutine called via `execute`, control
returns to the caller and the value is accessible as `return_value` in the caller's
context. In `main`, stops execution entirely (return value is discarded). To return
without a value, use `return: null`.
return.title: return

label.description:
Mark any point of the SWML section with a label so that `goto` can jump to it. Must be
unique within the section.

ReplyText.description:
Reply body text, used by the string shorthand and by string outcomes of an inline
`switch`. After variable expansion it must contain at least one non-whitespace
character.

Body length is checked before the reply is queued. The limit depends on the messaging
route used and on whether the reply is SMS or MMS, and length is counted according to
the message encoding. A body over the limit fails the reply.
ReplyText.title: Reply body text

to.description: Destination phone number in E.164 format. Defaults to the inbound message's `from`.

from.description: Sending phone number or short code. Must be owned by your project and have messaging capability. Defaults to the inbound message's `to`.

status_url.description:
HTTP or HTTPS URL that receives delivery status callbacks for the outbound reply. The
callback uses the [message status callback payload](/docs/apis/rest/webhooks/message-status-callback).
Callbacks are delivered after the reply is queued, so a `queued` result does not confirm
that a callback reached this URL.

body.description:
Body text of the reply. Required if `media` is not present. When no media is attached,
the body must contain at least one non-whitespace character after variable expansion.

Body length is checked before the reply is queued. The limit depends on the messaging
route used and on whether the reply is SMS or MMS, and length is counted according to
the message encoding. A body over the limit fails the reply.

media.description:
Array of HTTP or HTTPS media URLs to attach. Converts the message to MMS. Maximum 8
attachments. Media is fetched after the reply is queued, so a `queued` result does not
confirm that the media could be retrieved.

to.description: Destination phone number in E.164 format. Defaults to the inbound message's `from`.

from.description: Sending phone number or short code. Must be owned by your project and have messaging capability. Defaults to the inbound message's `to`.

status_url.description:
HTTP or HTTPS URL that receives delivery status callbacks for the outbound reply. The
callback uses the [message status callback payload](/docs/apis/rest/webhooks/message-status-callback).
Callbacks are delivered after the reply is queued, so a `queued` result does not confirm
that a callback reached this URL.

media.description:
Array of HTTP or HTTPS media URLs to attach. Converts the message to MMS. Required if
`body` is not present, and must then contain at least one URL. Maximum 8 attachments.
Media is fetched after the reply is queued, so a `queued` result does not confirm that
the media could be retrieved.

body.description:
Optional body text included alongside the media attachments. Must be a non-empty string
if provided. Body length is checked before the reply is queued; the limit depends on the
messaging route used and length is counted according to the message encoding.

variable.description: Variable path to match. Specified without the `%{}` wrapper (e.g. `message.body`).

transform.description: Transform to apply to the value before matching.

case.description:
Map of values to reply outcomes. Each entry's value is either a string (used as
the reply body, sent back to the original sender as SMS) or a full reply object
(`body`, `media`, `to`, `from`, `status_url`). Use the object form when the
branch needs media, a different destination, or a per-branch `status_url`.

default.description:
Fallback used when no `case` value matches. Same string-or-reply-object shape as a
`case` value. If omitted and no case matches, the `reply` step fails and execution
stops.

ReplyInlineSwitch.description:
Branch the reply on a variable value. The matched `case` (or `default`) supplies the
reply contents in one of two forms:

- **String** — sent back to the original sender as the SMS body. The simplest form,
  good for choosing between canned text responses.
- **Reply object** — a full `{ body, media, to, from, status_url }` block, so the
  matched branch can attach media, override the destination, or set a per-branch
  status callback. Any `%{…}` placeholders inside the object are expanded before
  the reply is sent.

When you use an inline `switch`, do not set `body`, `media`, `to`, `from`, or
`status_url` directly on the same `reply` — put them inside each `case` value
(or `default`) instead.
ReplyInlineSwitch.title: Reply with inline switch

SwitchTransform.description: Transform applied to the variable value before matching.
SwitchTransform.title: SwitchTransform enum

MessagingVariableReference.description:
A messaging SWML variable reference, such as `%{params.max_retries}`. It is replaced with
the variable's value from the inbound message (`message.*`), the current `params`, or a
variable set by an earlier step before the method uses it.
MessagingVariableReference.title: Messaging variable reference
